forecasts.reason: Early 20 px steps are host-bound at ~12 ms each, so this should save another ~0.15 s. But the cut is now eating into the LR warm-up the stem needs, so the second dose costs more than the first (~-0.15 pp). Seeds 0-2 are a coin flip at the 0.753 bar.

Group 3 runs on tiny 7/3 px maps where per-step cost is mostly launch and fixed work, so cutting its MACs saves only ~0.13 s. A 100-way head is capacity-limited late in the net (~-0.3 pp), which puts the rate below the dial at ~0.5 s/pp.
Group 1 learns until ~75% (E037/E055), so removing depth costs about what removing steps does. Expect ≥0.3 pp lost for a time cut of about 3.5%, short of the 5% the hypothesis needs.
On my host-bound view, 24→20 px saves little per step (E040 saved ~0.12 s). The fresh-seed loss is ~0.1 pp, which is within noise, so the gate is a coin flip.

Strong LS likely works together with Lookahead averaging to calibrate the end point, and E032 hurt. Lowering LS shrinks that implicit regularization, so expect flat to slightly negative, not ≥+0.2 pp.

cruxes: Is the 20/24 px step host-bound? Compare CUDA-event GPU time with wall time per step: if wall time is about 2x GPU time, step removal and per-step host-overhead cuts (fewer param-group loops, fusing the 3 Muon calls into one) are the cheapest remaining levers, and pixel or width cuts are not.
Does the early-trim dose curve stay flat past 225 steps, or does it fall off a cliff once the 20 px phase stops covering the LR warm-up (peak at 23% of steps)?
Is LS 0.3 coupled to Lookahead end-point averaging, so that it cannot be tuned independently?
structured_output.world_model: W5 (contrarian), after E061. Accuracy noise: per-seed SD is about 0.25 pp and the build SD is about 0. A tip whose population mean is ~0.7535 passes seeds 0-2 about half the time. Mechanism I hold: early and small-map steps are bound by host and fixed per-step work (Python loops over 9 groups, 3 Muon cudagraph calls, fused SGD, Lookahead), not by pixels. So step removal saves ~12 ms per step at any resolution, while pixel, width or depth cuts on small maps save less than FLOP accounting predicts. Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers that are still learning; freezes are free only after learning finishes. The next cheap lever is probably the host overhead itself: fuse the Muon groups into one compiled call and set LRs from a GPU schedule tensor. That is math-identical and could save ~0.1-0.3 s.
